chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said in a speech of his: 'Fear the evil ones of the women, and become cautious upon their good ones, and if they were to instruct you with the goodness, so oppose them so they would not expect obedience from you regarding the evil'.
ai.seo_question: Why should men oppose their wives even when they command good?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia scholarly concept of 'khulw' (strategic non-compliance) to maintain marital balance and prevent wives from becoming accustomed to commanding their husbands. It underscores the dynamic where even righteous commands are met with gentle resistance to preserve the husband's authority and prevent escalation into disobedience. This reflects the broader jurisprudential principle of preserving hierarchy within the family structure while maintaining mutual respect.
